rationale: Merge Middlebury Resource Recovery Center, PurposeEnergy Minster, and PurposeEnergy South Burlington into PurposeEnergy. Quinbrook's portfolio hierarchy identifies PurposeEnergy as the acquired manager-level platform and each named facility as a project beneath it. Direct company, regulatory, municipal, and historical sources support the project identities and operating facts but do not support separate sponsor mandates or co-owners. The three project/SPV identities, material operating milestones, and direct sources are retained on the canonical PurposeEnergy record.

beforeImage.name: PurposeEnergy
beforeImage.description: PurposeEnergy develops, owns, and operates organics-to-energy infrastructure that converts food and beverage waste into biogas, renewable electricity, renewable natural gas, clean water, and related by-products. Its customers are food and beverage manufacturers, breweries, processors, and other industrial waste generators that need onsite or near-site treatment and energy recovery. The operating model is asset-heavy and based on anaerobic digestion and related treatment infrastructure tied to industrial waste streams. Company materials state that the platform has developed, owned, and operated multiple projects over the last 15 years. Quinbrook acquired PurposeEnergy in 2023 as its entry platform in renewable fuels.

afterImage.name: PurposeEnergy
afterImage.description: PurposeEnergy develops, owns and operates organics-to-energy infrastructure that converts food and beverage residuals and wastewater into biogas, renewable electricity, renewable natural gas, clean water and related by-products. Quinbrook announced its acquisition of the platform on April 12, 2023 through its Net Zero Power Fund strategy; a separate legal closing date, exact stake and holding vehicle were not publicly disclosed. PurposeEnergy's project portfolio includes Middlebury Resource Recovery Center in Vermont, which reached commercial operation on October 21, 2024; the Minster, Ohio industrial-biogas facility, which began taking waste on July 16, 2026 and remained in ramp-up; and the operating South Burlington, Vermont brewery-waste digester historically associated with Magic Hat and now Zero Gravity. These facility and SPV names are project identities beneath PurposeEnergy and are not separate manager-level portfolio companies. No later PurposeEnergy equity transfer or signed pending sale was identified through September 1, 2026.
